es: Escribir una queja exagerada y una respuesta bromista con so/such… that, un correlativo y suavizadores que mantengan el buen tono.

teaching.en: I do not want to exaggerate, but this suitcase weighs a million kilos.
teaching.es: No quiero exagerar, pero esta maleta pesa un millón de kilos.
teaching.explanationEs: Exagerar de forma evidente es hipérbole: nadie cree que pese tanto.

teaching.en: My complaint is simple: this sofa is so hard that I sleep on the floor.
teaching.es: Mi queja es simple: este sofá es tan duro que duermo en el suelo.
teaching.explanationEs: So + adjetivo + that + resultado: intensidad con una consecuencia exagerada.
segments: My complaint is simple: this sofa is so
hard that I sleep on the floor.

teaching.en: Both my brother and my sister forgot my birthday, and I am kind of hurt. I am only joking!
teaching.es: Mi hermano y mi hermana olvidaron mi cumpleaños, y estoy un poco dolido. ¡Es broma!
teaching.explanationEs: Kind of y I am only joking suavizan: avisan de que es una broma.

teaching.explanationEs: Either… or ofrece dos opciones; la alternativa exagerada busca el humor.

teaching.explanationEs: Neither… nor significa «ni… ni» y lleva el verbo en afirmativo.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que exagera con so… that para hacer reír.

choices.text: The queue was long, so I waited for ten minutes.
The queue was longer than the one on Monday.
The queue was so long that I learned to play the guitar.

feedback.es: Solo la frase con so + adjetivo y un resultado absurdo exagera; las otras describen o comparan sin exagerar.

hint.es: Busca intensidad (so + adjetivo) seguida de un resultado imposible.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi bolso pesa tanto que creo que lleva un caballo.»

feedback.es: Delante de un adjetivo solo (heavy) se usa so: so heavy that…

hint.es: No va seguido de «a + nombre», sino de un adjetivo.

origin.text: My bag is ___ heavy that I think it contains a horse.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ni la pizza ni la ensalada estaban listas.»

feedback.es: Neither se completa siempre con nor: «ni… ni».

hint.es: Es la pareja de neither; juntas significan «ni… ni».

origin.text: Neither the pizza ___ the salad was ready.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que bromea sin ofender sobre la cena de Ana.

choices.text: Kind of a disaster? I am only joking: it smells great!
Your cooking is always a disaster, Ana.
Nobody could eat that, not even the dog.

feedback.es: La respuesta con kind of y I am only joking suaviza; las otras atacan la cocina de Ana.

origin.text: Ana says, “I cooked dinner for ten people, and it was a disaster.” Her friend answers:

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tanto mi hermano como mi hermana olvidaron las llaves.»

answer.text: Both my brother and my sister forgot the keys

feedback.es: Both… and une dos sujetos y el verbo va en plural: both my brother and my sister forgot.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la hablante con su comentario.

choices.text: She is seriously worried about a horse.
She exaggerates and then shows she is joking.
She is angry and wants to complain to the airline.

feedback.es: Exagera con so heavy that y cierra con kind of y I am only joking: hipérbole con suavizador.

origin.audio: This suitcase is so heavy that I think it has a small horse inside. Kind of. I am only joking.

prompt.es: Escribe una queja exagerada y una respuesta bromista con so/such y un correlativo.

answer.text: My complaint is simple: the bus was so late that I grew old at the stop. It was such a cold morning that my coffee turned into ice cream, and both my phone and my umbrella stopped working. Either the bus company is on holiday, or the driver is lost in another city. I am kind of angry, but I am only joking. My friend Leo answered: Poor you! You are so funny that I could sell tickets to your show. Neither the bus nor the weather is your fault, but either you leave home earlier, or I buy you a bicycle. Kind of. Seriously, come to my house and I will make you a hot chocolate. We can complain about the bus together, and I promise to laugh only a little.
accepted: My complaint is simple: the bus was so late that I grew old at the stop. It was such a cold morning that my coffee turned into ice cream, and both my phone and my umbrella stopped working. Either the bus company is on holiday, or the driver is lost in another city. I am kind of angry, but I am only joking. My friend Leo answered: Poor you! You are so funny that I could sell tickets to your show. Neither the bus nor the weather is your fault, but either you leave home earlier, or I buy you a bicycle. Kind of. Seriously, come to my house and I will make you a hot chocolate. We can complain about the bus together, and I promise to laugh only a little.

My complaint is simple: the queue at the supermarket was so long that I read a whole book in it. It was such a slow day that the cashier needed a map to find the bread, and both the milk and the eggs were at the other end of the shop. Either they open more tills, or I move into the car park. I am sort of tired, but I am just joking. My friend Mia answered: You are so brave that you deserve a medal. Neither the cashier nor the bread is your enemy, but either you go early, or I do the shopping for you. Kind of. Seriously, come for dinner and I will cook pasta. We can complain about the queue together, and I promise to laugh only a little.

feedback.es: La respuesta completa exagera con so/such… that, usa un correlativo y mantiene el buen tono con un suavizador.

origin.text: Escribe unas 120–200 palabras en inglés. Parte 1: una queja exagerada sobre algo cotidiano (una cola, un atasco, un autobús). Parte 2: la respuesta bromista de un amigo. Usa dos estructuras de intensidad (so… that / such a… that), un correlativo (both… and, either… or o neither… nor) y un suavizador (kind of, I am only joking).

prompt.es: Elige la frase que exagera con gracia sin herir a nadie.

choices.text: Mia sings so badly that she should stop forever.
Mia is such a useless singer that nobody can stand her.
Mia sings so loudly that the neighbours' dogs ask for silence!

feedback.es: La frase de los perros exagera de forma absurda y cariñosa; las otras insultan a Mia aunque también usen so o such.

origin.text: Your friend Mia sings in the kitchen every morning. You write her a funny note.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ni el autobús ni el tren llegaron a tiempo.»

answer.text: Neither the bus nor the train arrived on time

feedback.es: Neither… nor lleva el verbo en afirmativo: arrived, no «did not arrive».

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje y elige qué hace la hablante.

choices.text: She jokes that she misses her devices a lot.
She is angry at the toaster for breaking.
She is calling a shop about her phone.

feedback.es: «So lost… that I am talking to the toaster» es una hipérbole y kind of la suaviza.

origin.audio: Both my phone and my laptop died this morning. I am so lost without them that I am talking to the toaster. Kind of.

prompt.es: Completa: «O me ayudas con las maletas, o me voy sola.»

feedback.es: Either se combina con or: «o… o». Abre una de las dos opciones.

origin.text: ___ you help me with the bags, or I go alone.

prompt.es: ¿Qué añadido convierte «Your idea is silly» en una broma amable?

choices.text: Kind of silly, but I am only joking!
Your idea is so silly that nobody will help.

feedback.es: Kind of y I am only joking son los suavizadores; repetir la crítica o exagerarla contra la idea no suaviza nada.

feedback.es: Both suma dos elementos, so… that une intensidad y resultado, la hipérbole exagera y el softener suaviza.
